# Synvy Neuro Mobile App - Health Tracking App UI

# Client Pain

Synvy reached out when their wellness app started feeling heavier than it should. Users were jumping between screens just to find basic info, insights took forever to surface, and the team was drowning in manual stuff that should've been automated ages ago. The interface couldn't keep up with how fast they were growing, and you could feel it.

# About the Project

Synvy is a stress-tracking app that helps people actually understand what's going on with their nervous system. It pulls together biometric data, AI analysis, and real-time feedback into one calm, focused space, so instead of staring at numbers, you get clarity. Less noise, more control over how you feel.

...

We needed to take everything scattered across the platform and bring it home. One dashboard. One flow. Fewer taps to get to what matters. The goal wasn't just to make it look nice, it was to build something that could grow with the product without falling apart.

...

# Key Decisions

We pulled all the core health metrics into a single dashboard, so nothing important is more than a glance away. Cut the screen-hopping. Softened the visual language to match what the app is actually about: calm, recovery, and slowing down. The glass textures and muted blues aren't decoration; they set the tone before you even read anything.

...

After launch, the numbers backed up the feeling. Time-to-insight dropped by around 40%, daily active usage went up 28%, and user retention at the 30-day mark improved by nearly a third. The team cut manual operations roughly in half, which freed them up to actually build instead of firefighting. As the founder put it: "We finally see the whole picture — and we move faster because of it."

# MRT Pass — Dhaka Metro Rail Card Manager

A dark, minimal Flatter app that reads your MRT Pass card balance and journey history via NFC — no login, no account, just tap and go.

The idea started simple: I wanted to check my metro card balance without carrying it to a machine. One tap of the phone on the card, and the app reads everything directly; balance, last trips, fares.

All offline. All instant.

The visual language is built around depth and restraint. Deep navy backgrounds, soft cyan glows and five handcrafted gradient card themes that feel like actual physical cards — Ocean, Midnight, Violet, Forest, Ember.

Every card has a perspective-transformed 3D carousel on the home screen. The cards tilt and scale as you swipe, giving a satisfying sense of physicality to something that's entirely digital.

The balance counter animates from zero to the actual amount every time you open a card. A small detail, but it makes the number feel earned.

The NFC scan screen uses three concentric pulsing rings that breathe in and out, guiding the user to hold their card. When reading succeeds, the rings snap to green. When it fails, red. No confusion about what happened.

The fare calculator has a live metro line visualization. The two selected stations highlight with glowing dots, and a small train icon pulses at each one. The route between them lights up in cyan.

Typography is tight and deliberate — 9-character section labels in all-caps with wide letter-spacing, heavy weight balances, and fine caption text that sits back without disappearing.

Home: 3D card carousel, quick scan shortcuts, recent activity feed

Card Detail: animated balance, monthly stats, full trip history

NFC Scan: pulsing ring UI, live feedback states

Fare Calculator: visual metro line, swap animation, savings badge

Analytics: mini bar charts per card, monthly breakdowns
